svg.title: Information value and novelty are separable: a human category contrast and an abbreviated macaque information-choice task
svg.desc: Panel A, humans: three equal option cards with different abstract patterns. The first two are grouped as seen before; the third is not seen before. Card one is familiar with payoff sampled, marked by a small history-sheet icon. Card two is familiar with payoff uncertain and card three is novel with payoff uncertain; both carry matching question-mark icons. Two comparison rows follow: uncertainty-directed sampling, with a calendar icon, is sensitive to future usefulness; novelty preference, with an end-marker icon, persists near the end. A footnote reads conceptual contrast; illustrative symbols. Panel B, macaques: from a choice node, choose a target, two routes of equal length. The informative route, tagged preferred, leads to one of two alternative cue cards, large or small, each followed after a delay by the matching water reward, shown as the same cup with a high or low water level. The uninformative route leads to a box labeled random cue containing the same two illustrative shapes separated by or. On each trial one of the two shapes is selected pseudorandomly without a consistent shape-to-reward mapping, followed after the same delay by either the large or the small reward. The two shapes inside this box are alternatives, not simultaneous stimuli; all cue symbols are schematic substitutes for the original stimuli. A brace at right labels the outcomes of both routes as the same reward distribution. A footnote reads abbreviated task. Arrows show task order and possible contingencies only; or-branches are alternative trials.
